cases.notes: The first line is a paragraph; the second starts a prefix-form definition list.
Blocks owned by a ListItem are not independently addressable; an inner paragraph ID is semantically invalid.
Task recognition is restricted to ordered/unordered list items; task-shaped text after : remains term content.
A heading is not in the §9.8 closed set of structured list-item children; the parser rejects it rather than silently ending the list.
A thematic break is not a permitted structured child of a list item (§9.8).

0.1.0 uses a uniform list model with no tight/loose distinction (§9.15/§9.19). A blank line between simple-list items does not split the list; it is a tolerated normal-mode surface, removed in the canonical form, rejected by strict. Two adjacent same-kind lists have no canonical surface (EVOLUTION_V053_TO_010.md §A12).
Ordered lists merge across a blank line the same way; the ordinals stay consecutive so no visible deviation is recorded.
The bullet character (`-`/`+`/`*`) is not semantic in 0.1.0 (§9.2), so a CommonMark bullet change that would start a new list is absorbed into the same uniform list.
